name: The Age of Calamity
era_span: The Age of Calamity, which all four cards name and WORLD.md files under "Fit none". This record puts it on no count and gives no year. Sinclair's card sets the Guild Accord's institutions inside his life (the Sanctum Lux censor rolls, the Research and Archives Division, the Bureau of Strategic Assessment, Enforcement teams with a Sealwright); the Harmonic, Sage and Spirit Rune Arts pages order the age before the Voyager Era; c05 reads the Wandering Fang's Age of Calamity as later than the Academy years. None of the three events needs the Accord, and none settles where the age falls. Order: the Bloodspine ground; the days under the Fractured Crown, days later on the same ground; the second Crown, later, on another stretch of the same steps. All three stand on the flood-basalt steps at the Crevice margin in the Outer World.

members.line: The Arbiter of Unity, the Veilborn Ascendant, wielder of Hikariken. A hybrid of Yukari and high elven blood, trained under a Yukari mentor-sect and then among the Veilwalkers of Vellsorea (the New World, the Eastern Rise), "claimed as a full son by neither"; unaffiliated. His Catalyst: "He severed the Astral Gate at the Shattering of Virelion", carried "as references only". He refuses "To be claimed". He reads by what is missing and sees planar seams; his cut opens a seam in the ground under wards, Domains and running techniques, and its light "does not illuminate". During the cut he empties toward whatever is nearest, and he has hospitalised two people so and calls both accidents. Hikariken is formed at need, with no scabbard. He speaks a learned Eressean, too correct. He does not know whether the seams close.

Bearer of the Fractured Crown. Human, Creviceborne (an exposure lineage), "Unaligned. Former Scion of the Outer Crevice". He walked into a Crevice-margin concentration, stayed coherent long enough to choose how he met it, and came out; "Something did not finish leaving with him." Trapped at Dissonance. Near him certainty thins into anger, and he cannot switch it off; wounds from his hands close slow, and plate turns that touch. He grows worse the longer a fight runs, and at sustained peak a lattice forms over his head, larger to those who see it twice. His Domain seals escape and decays over days after he leaves. His signature needs him still through the build and cannot be aimed; afterward he is slower for a week and does not sleep for three nights. His desire is "To finish". Nobody knows why the Crevice let him leave.

The Soul Devourer, the Sculptor of the Echoed Dead; in the Sanctum Lux censor rolls "the Cannibal", the one name he objects to. Half-mortal of Abythron, offered to Zar'thuun and declined; formerly of the Spiral Covenant. He feeds a hunger he believes has a bottom, and the count he keeps has not gone down. Essence bleeds toward him without his acting, and being asked to stop it angers him. What he takes becomes constructs with their owners' temper; his shadow has not obeyed him in years; his Domain, the Unwritten Grave, keeps his dead present. Weak to radiant current and to sustained physical trauma; twice a Sealwright team took him from behind Chainsalt, and both times he left. Courteous, and does not enjoy killing. He dresses in out-of-date Abythron wool and mends it himself. His lost Spirit Axis is a gap his card keeps on purpose; Tilda is his one recorded failure.

The Magmaborn Juggernaut, Warden of the Broken Spires, Herald of Bloodfire. Orc of the Bloodspine clan, deep-earth volcanic strain; last surviving chieftain of the Bloodspine line and vanguard for the deep resistance fronts. A soul furnace trial in his youth took eleven of them; afterward, young, he made the wound structure, and near death his blood calcifies into obsidian around the vital organs. Nobody knows whether the obsidian is his. His signature drives his fists into stone and finds where it was already going to break; on sand, bog or a deck it does nothing, and after it he runs cold for a day and a half. He cannot chase, and commanders who beat him choose where. He refuses to be moved off ground he has committed to, and the rest of his clan died where he had decided to stand. Monosyllables; no trust for abstractions.

events.name: The Bloodspine ground
events.when: The Age of Calamity. After Iskaron came out of the Crevice-margin concentration (his Catalyst Event) and after Gorrath made his blood into structure (his); Gorrath was chieftain of the Bloodspine.
events.where: The flood-basalt steps at the Crevice margin, in the Outer World (WORLD §5, South; the Outer World page's flood-basalt terraces and columnar Trapstone). No stretch is named; the Broken Spires stay unplaced.
events.what: New. The Bloodspine held the basalt steps above the margin, and Iskaron came up out of the margin onto them; they stood across his way. Near him their certainty thinned and they reached for anger, and it was there. His bare hands opened them and the wounds would not knit; on Gorrath they found obsidian plate. Gorrath drove both fists into the basalt; the rupture ran down the joints of the columns and molten chain-spikes came up through the cracks. Iskaron took it and kept coming, worse at the end than at the start. Then he stopped moving and a lattice formed above his head. Gorrath had not seen the stillness before and did not step back, and the Bloodspine stayed where their chieftain stood. The air went wrong, sound came late, the columns came apart at their joints. Gorrath's blood went to obsidian and he lived. Iskaron walked off the steps; his Domain stayed on the basalt, decaying, with the wounded Bloodspine inside it. Took: Gorrath, most of his clan dead on the ground he chose and the rest dying on it, a day and a half of cold, the stillness seen once; Iskaron, a man he could not open or finish, a week slower and three nights sleepless, a witness to the lattice.

events.name: The days under the Fractured Crown
events.when: The days after the Bloodspine ground, while Iskaron's Domain decayed on the basalt.
events.where: The same flood-basalt steps at the Crevice margin, in the Outer World.
events.what: New. Iskaron was gone; his Domain was there. While it lay over the ground a withdrawal was hard to work and an escape went unanswered, so the dying could only be carried, and the one man left would not leave the ground. Sinclair came on foot in his dark wool coat; Gorrath saw only a shadow that did not match the man above it. Sinclair knelt beside each of the dying Bloodspine in turn, courteous, and one by one they stopped; he took them without hurrying. Gorrath went at him over the fallen columns, and each time he arrived Sinclair was somewhere other than in front of him; he did not leave the ground to chase. Where the Crevice runs, the Crown had shut the bleed between the planes, and Zarron, who reads by what is missing, came to it. He stood alone at the Crown's edge and cut; a seam opened in the basalt, the Crown's boundary took another shape, and the light off the seam lit nothing. He came onto the steps with Hikariken in his hand, and Sinclair stood up and left before the light was off the seam. None of the Bloodspine lived to morning. Gorrath pried basalt posts loose by hand and stood them over his dead; Zarron carried posts with him until the last cairn was up, then went. Took: Sinclair, the dying of the Bloodspine and fragments with their temper, kept in his Chainsalt coffer, the count risen, a radiant blade he left before; Zarron, a Domain cut unseen and its maker's shape read from what it left out, a seam he cannot read, cairns raised beside a man who distrusts abstractions; Gorrath, the rest of his clan taken by a man he could not catch, cairns of basalt, a seam in that ground; Iskaron, absent, his Domain cut by a stranger and the dying he left taken by another.

events.name: The second Crown
events.when: Later in the Age of Calamity, after the Bloodspine ground, when Gorrath stood as vanguard for one of the deep resistance fronts (his card's standing).
events.where: Another stretch of the flood-basalt steps at the Crevice margin, in the Outer World.
events.what: New. The front held the steps with Gorrath at its head, and Iskaron came up out of the margin again. The fight went long. When Iskaron stopped moving, Gorrath had seen that stillness once; he sent the front back off the steps, and they went, and he stayed on the ground alone. The lattice formed above Iskaron's head, larger than on the Bloodspine ground. The air went wrong and the columns under Gorrath came apart at their joints; his blood went to obsidian again and he lived. The front lived, off the steps. Iskaron walked away down the margin. Took: Gorrath, a front alive behind him, the lattice seen twice (he is one of the witnesses who report it larger the second time), his ground broken under him again; Iskaron, the same man twice unfinished, a witness who has seen the lattice twice, a week slower and three nights sleepless.

ties.summary: Iskaron killed the Bloodspine on the basalt where Gorrath had decided to stand and did not finish him; on another stretch of the steps Gorrath sent his front back, stood alone, and saw the lattice larger.
Sinclair took the dying Bloodspine off the ground Gorrath held, one at a time, and was never in front of him when he arrived.

Zarron cut the Fractured Crown on the Bloodspine ground and came in with Hikariken, and the man taking the dying left; he carried basalt with Gorrath until the last cairn was up, and his seam is in that ground.

Zarron came onto the Bloodspine steps with Hikariken while Sinclair knelt among the dying, and Sinclair left before the light was off the seam; radiant current is the weakness Sinclair's card names first.
Zarron cut the Domain Iskaron left on the Bloodspine ground and read its maker's shape from what it left out; his cut undoes what the Fractured Crown holds shut.
Sinclair walked into the Domain Iskaron left on the basalt and took the dying his hands had left there; they have never met, and both are trapped at Dissonance.

outward.wants: One of the two people he has hospitalised through his cut and "describes both as accidents" (his card, VII): an ally who was nearest when he cut and took what he gave whether or not they wanted it. No card names either, and neither was on the Bloodspine ground.

A physician who has treated wounds from his hands beside wounds from anything else, one of his card's "physicians who have treated both can tell the difference without being told" (IV); perhaps someone who worked the fronts at the margin and never met him.
A Sanctum Lux censor who interviewed him: the rolls that call him the Cannibal, "the only name he has ever objected to" (I), and the censor who came away with "the same note in the margin" (XIV).

A commander who has beaten him by choosing where (his card, VIII): someone who put him on loose ground or let him arrive "somewhere that does not matter" (VI), on his own side of the fronts or across them.

card_contradictions: Iskaron's Tempering. Zarron's card: "Compare Iskaron at 495", and "this is why Zarron is Refined and Iskaron is Overgrown" (Zarron, IV). Iskaron's card gives his Tempering as 383, "Two Grades under his Ardency. This is the Overgrown state stated as a number" (Iskaron, II-b).

Whether Sinclair loses three sub-stats. Gorrath's card: "Sinclair loses three sub-stats to the Obsession question." (Gorrath, V). Sinclair's card: three sub-stats "clear Attraction Path commitment through Obsession Force and hold at the values below" (Sinclair, IV). RULINGS.md, 2026-09-12: "Obsession Force satisfies an Attraction Path gate the same way clean Attraction Force does". Isaac's ruling governs; Gorrath's card still carries the older line.

Refined as the exception. Zarron's card: "Crystal State · Refined. Rare among the Volume III cast and worth noting as the exception." (Zarron, II). Gorrath's card, from the same volume: "Crystal State · Refined." (Gorrath, II).

Within Sinclair's card. Its stat table gives Resilience 572 and Vitality 328 (IV); its physical-force section: "His Resilience sits at 742 and his Vitality at 426" (VI); its sub-stat notes: "Six stats sit above 700, which is the Stage XI fracture line" (V), where the highest figure in its tables is 578.

Card against wiki, when the age falls. Sinclair's card sets inside his life "the Sanctum Lux censor rolls", "the Bureau of Strategic Assessment", "The Research and Archives Division" and "a Sealwright team" (Sinclair, I, VII, X). wiki/The Disciplines/The Harmonic Arts.md: "The Age of Calamity weaponized all three", followed by "By the Voyager Era the Harmonic Arts occupy a dual status"; the Sage Arts and Spirit Rune Arts pages order the age the same way, before the era that founded the Accord (WORLD §1). c05 reads the Wandering Fang's Age of Calamity as later than the Academy years (c05, section 7, item 9).
